It's understandable to feel worried when you see these changes in your son. While some withdrawal and private time can be typical during adolescence, prolonged isolation, talking to oneself, and laughing without an apparent trigger could signal something that deserves professional attention. These behaviors can be associated with several conditions—or they could reflect stress, anxiety, or another emotional struggle—so it's important not to jump to conclusions.

The best next step would be to have a gentle, nonjudgmental conversation with your son about how he's been feeling, and to reach out to a mental health professional or his pediatrician for a proper evaluation. Early support can make a meaningful difference, whatever the underlying cause may be. You're clearly caring and observant, and seeking guidance is the right thing to do. If you ever notice signs of immediate risk—such as self-harm or thoughts of suicide—please contact emergency services or a crisis line right away.
